questions.question: What does Chapter 3 say about sovereign debt in developing economies?
questions.tests: a summary question over a 36-page chapter
questions.answer: Chapter 3 states that rising government debt poses a key challenge for emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs) because it leads to higher interest rates, higher debt-service payments, and a greater likelihood of debt distress. Debt levels are positively associated with dollar-denominated sovereign bond spreads and domestic-currency government bond yields, and this relationship is non-linear so that increases in spreads or yields associated with increases in debt-to-GDP ratios are greater the higher the debt-to-GDP ratio. The rise in EMDE debt-to-GDP ratios since 2010 is associated with increases in sovereign spreads and domestic-currency yields of about 110 and 30 basis points, respectively. Between 2010 and 2024, median EMDE debt rose by 20 percentage points of GDP, which model estimates indicate added 114 basis points to sovereign spreads and 31 basis points to domestic-currency yields.

questions.question: What does Chapter 3 say about sovereign debt in developing economies?
questions.tests: a summary question over a 36-page chapter
missing: 1 more of: spread|yield|interest rate / non-linear|nonlinear|greater the higher / 110|basis points / default|credit rating|frontier|governance|short-term debt / fiscal
questions.answer: Chapter 3 explores the impact of government debt on interest rates in emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs), finding that debt levels are positively associated with dollar-denominated sovereign bond spreads and domestic-currency government bond yields. The rise in EMDE debt-to-GDP ratios since 2010 is associated with increases in sovereign spreads and domestic-currency yields of about 110 and 30 basis points, respectively. Between 2010 and 2024, advanced economy government debt increased by an average of about 12 percentage points of GDP, which alongside the rise in domestic EMDE debt implies a total rise in yields of 149 and 40 basis points, respectively. The chapter only partially addresses sovereign debt as it focuses specifically on its relationship with interest rates and bond yields.
